questions.prompt: Why does `SELECT * FROM tasks WHERE completed_at = NULL` return ZERO rows even when NULL rows exist?

options.text: In SQL three-valued logic, `= NULL` evaluates to `UNKNOWN` rather than `TRUE`; you must write `IS NULL`
PostgreSQL hides NULL rows by default
The `=` operator works only on integers
Dates cannot contain NULL

questions.explanation: SQL requires `IS NULL` / `IS NOT NULL` because NULL denotes missing unknown state, not equality.

questions.prompt: If you can filter active records using either `WHERE active = true` or putting `active = true` inside `HAVING`, which performs far better on large tables?

options.text: `WHERE` runs before grouping and can utilize B-Tree indexes directly, cutting memory and aggregation cost
`HAVING` always runs faster
They execute identical plans regardless of size
SQL ignores `WHERE` when `GROUP BY` is present

questions.explanation: Push row-level filters into WHERE early to shrink intermediate rows prior to aggregation.
